correctness.rationale: For the triangle, P=(3I+J)/6 where J is all ones. The row sums of PB are at most 5/6 with the third platform susceptibility zero, so the fixed point is attracting even at z=1. Solving the two active equations, then the third, gives y=(1-b)(8-5z,2,2-z)/D, D=12-8b-8z+5bz>=1. The three pairwise squared differences divided by 9 give population variance about its own mean. Its derivative has sign of (12-11b)z-12(1-b), giving the claimed unique interior minimum and strict sign change. Substitution confirms the minimum and both endpoint gaps; for example the frozen increase at b=3/4 is exactly 1/1274. The two-agent centered eigenvalue of P is 1-2alpha; writing y=P u and solving the two anchor equations gives the absolute gap coefficient |1-2alpha|/[1+alpha(b/(1-b)+c/(1-c))]. Squaring and dividing by 4 confirms coordinatewise nonincrease. If one susceptibility is 1 the other anchors a consensus; both 1 allow multiple equilibria, all consensuses, and the variance remains zero. One agent has variance zero. This establishes sharpness in the stated class, not with arbitrary prediction/peer rules. As the third stiffness tends to infinity with zero innate opinion, its coordinate vanishes, and the two retained rows give the grounded baseline M=[[k+1/3,-1/6],[-1/6,1/3]], invertible since det(M)=q/12. Thus the indexed baseline solution and resolvent column become u_0=k(4,2,0)/q and v=(2,12k+4,0)/q. All inverse and response coefficients converge by the block inverse formula.

originality.rationale: The pivotal optimization is a mechanical complete-graph specialization of a distinct indexed one-vertex FJ theorem, not just a similar path example. At a predictive fixed point write y=P u and u=(I-B)x*+BPu. On the frozen triangle L=I-P=(I-J/3)/2 is a symmetric weighted Laplacian, and the equation for u is the static FJ equation (L+K)u=Kx*, where K_ii=(1-beta_i)/beta_i; zero susceptibility pins u_i=x_i^*. The indexed combined objective becomes a positive constant multiple of the frozen pure variance because L is proportional to the centering projector, and P acts as 1/2 on that subspace. The indexed rank-one optimizer applies with the third vertex pinned by the explicit infinite-stubbornness limit and gives exactly z_b and the frozen bowl; details below. The one- and two-agent boundary in this setting is an elementary anchored opinion-gap computation, not a distinct surviving theorem of comparable scope. This decision credits indexed mathematical coverage, not chronological priority or dependence; the dates of the entries alone do not adjudicate those questions.
residual_risks: Bounded catalogue and primary-literature inspection is not a priority determination. In particular, the later catalogue date of the broader result is not used to assert that it was published first or that one record used the other.
